Damage: 1d8 piercing

Properties: F

Mastery: Vex

You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Whenever you roll an 8 on the damage die for an attack made with this weapon, the target takes an extra 1d8 Poison damage. In addition, when you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll made with this weapon against a creature, the target must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes 3d6 Poison damage and has the Poisoned condition for 1 minute. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only.

Weight: 6 lb.

Armour Class: 2

While holding this large Shield, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class. This bonus is in addition to the Shield's normal bonus to AC. The bonus becomes +2 while you have at least 1 Temporary Hit Point. While you have Temporary Hit Points, the Shield emits a slight blue glow.

In addition, you can channel the heroic resolve within the Shield as a Magic action to gain 1d6 + 8 Temporary Hit Points. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

This delicious gum comes in packs of five and can be blown into large, levitating bubbles 1 foot in diameter. You need to chew a piece of the gum for 1 minute before its magic can be used. Once it's been chewed for at least 1 minute, you can take a Magic action while the gum is in your mouth to blow a single bubble with it. When you do, you gain the effect of the Levitate spell, as if you had cast it, provided the bubble stays attached to the gum in your mouth. While the effect doesn't require your Concentration, it does end early and cause you to fall if you take an action to pop it or if the bubble takes any damage; the bubble is a loose object for the purpose of any attack or effect that would target it. The effect ends on its own after 10 minutes, allowing you and the bubble to float gently down to the ground if you're still aloft. The gum becomes nonmagical, albeit still delicious, once this bubble's effect ends.

When you take the Magic action to blow this bubble, you can remove it from your mouth as part of the same action and stick it on another creature or loose object within 5 feet of you. When you do, the stuck target gains the effect of the Levitate spell, instead of you, but you have no control over it; the effect otherwise functions as described above. An unwilling creature that succeeds on a DC 13 Dexterity saving throw avoids having the bubble stuck to it.

This pair of golden rings play a sad, sad melody when you rub the two fingers wearing them together. Creatures that know the Vicious Mockery cantrip can use this set of rings as a Somatic component for the spell instead of the normal Verbal component required by it.

This magic Quiver is made from the shell of an enormous oyster. Arrows you pull from it are magical and are coated with a pearlescent, hydrophobic coating. Ranged attack rolls made with these Arrows ignore the normal drawbacks of underwater combat. The Arrows become nonmagical once they hit a target or are held by a creature other than you.

Create Pearl

You can use a command word to cause the Quiver to create a magical pearl. You can hold onto this pearl or give it to another creature. When a creature with the pearl makes a Wisdom check or Wisdom saving throw, it can choose to make the check or save with Advantage. When it does, the pearl turns to dust. The pearl is visibly magical and disintegrates on its own after 24 hours if left unused. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

m: Wondrous item · Very Rare · needs attunement
h:
This magic silvered pendant glows with a simmering flame of rage trapped inside its clenched fist. Small sparks shoot out from between the pendant's metal fingers. The fiery anger from the pendant tightens your focus and allows you to shrug off some of the damage you take. If you aren't wearing armor or wielding a Shield while you wear this pendant, all Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage you take is reduced by 3.

In addition, the pendant has 3 charges and regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn. You can take a Bonus Action and expend 1 charge to ignite your hands in a magical flame, causing them to shed Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet. Whenever you deal damage with your Unarmed Strike while your hands are wreathed in this fire, it can deal your choice of Fire damage or its normal damage type, and it deals an extra 1d4 Fire damage on a hit. Your hands remain lit for 1 minute or until you take a Bonus Action to quench them.

Any flame created by the pendant, whether it be on your hands or on the pendant itself, is harmless to you.

While wearing this pendant, you know Thieves' Cant. In addition, you can more easily recognize the patterns used in linguistic codes, granting you a +5 bonus to Intelligence checks made to understand a written or spoken cipher.

This hard, minty sugarbomb slowly dissolves in your mouth over the course of 1 hour. At any point, you can take a Bonus Action to crunch down and break the sugarbomb into tiny, painful shards. You take 1d6 Piercing damage from the shards but are temporarily enchanted by the candy. Whenever you hit a target with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike that deals Piercing or Slashing damage while you're enchanted in this way, the target takes an extra 2 damage. This enchantment fades after 1 minute.

Upset Stomach

You can only be under the effects of one sugarbomb that has this property at a time. Eating a sugarbomb that has this property while under the effects of another one causes the effects of the first sugarbomb to immediately end and be replaced by the new one's. This rapid change is difficult to stomach, forcing you to make a DC 13 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you have the Poisoned condition for 1 minute.

This perfectly reflective charm magically helps you meditate and focus your mind. Whenever you fail an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw while wearing the necklace, you can take a Reaction to reroll the save, and you must use the new roll.

Curse

This periapt is cursed, a fact that is only revealed when the curse extends to you due to rolling a 1 on a saving throw after using the periapt to reroll it. Until the curse ends, the mirrored surface of the necklace dulls into an ugly, flat gray while you wear it. The curse persists even if you aren't wearing the necklace, and you remain cursed until you are targeted by a Remove Curse spell or similar magic.

While you're cursed, your reflection in any mirrored surface within 10 feet of you turns into an ugly, horrifying visage of your deepest insecurities. In addition, when you fail an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw (including the roll that reveals this curse), you take 1d8 Psychic damage.

This violet piece of parchment is smooth and pleasant to write on. You can take a Bonus Action and use either of the command words, "lock" or "unlock," to magically lock or unlock the parchment, respectively. While locked, the sheet can't be torn by hand, damaged by fire, or damaged by immersion in water, and any ink already on the page can't be removed, smeared, or otherwise changed without the use of magic. New ink added to a locked sheet of Permanent Parchment runs off the page like water. While unlocked, the parchment behaves like a nonmagical sheet of paper.

If the sheet is unlocked, you can use another command word, "clear," to cause any ink on the sheet of parchment to magically evaporate without leaving any marks behind.

This cape is made of colorful and aromatic petals. While wearing the cape, petals drift behind you as you walk and disappear before touching the ground. You can take a Bonus Action to magically change the color of these petals. While wearing the cape, you can cast the Druidcraft cantrip from it, and Beasts and Plant creatures have Disadvantage on Opportunity Attacks against you.

Weight: 4 lb.

Damage: 1d8 slashing (1d10 two-handed)

Properties: V, T

Mastery: Topple

This crystalline Battleaxe seems to be almost transparent when looking at the bladed head from different angles. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which has the Thrown property with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet. The first time on your turn when you hit a target with a ranged attack roll using the axe, you can force another creature within 10 feet of the target to make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, that creature takes 1d8 Force damage.

If you can see the axe and are within 60 feet of it, you can take a Bonus Action to magically return the axe to your outstretched hand. When you do, the weapon phases through any obstacle in its path that isn't more than 5 feet thick or made of lead.

Weight: 18 lb.

Damage: 1d10 piercing

Properties: H, R, 2H

Mastery: Push

You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The weapon has 6 charges and regains 1d4 + 2 expended charges daily at dusk. While holding this Pike, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 17) from it: Mirror Image (1 charge), Phantom Steed (1 charge), Speak with Dead (1 charge), or Spirit Guardians (2 charges).

Spectral Warrior

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with this Pike, you can choose to summon a spectral warrior from it. Until the start of your next turn, the target is haunted by this warrior, causing it to have Disadvantage on attack rolls against you. This property has no effect against Undead creatures.

Haunting Phalanx

You can take a Magic action while holding this Pike to expend 3 charges and point it forward commandingly. Five spectral, Pike-wielding warriors appear before you and march in a 25-foot-wide, 50-foot-long Line in a direction you choose. Any creature within the area must make a DC 17 Intelligence saving throw; Undead creatures automatically succeed on the save. On a failed save, a target takes 3d10 Necrotic damage and 3d10 Psychic damage and is affected by the weapon's Spectral Warrior property. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only.

This birdlike mask's blend of magic and science is as unique as it is helpful. While wearing it, you can easily lift it above your face to eat or speak more clearly. The mask's beak is lined with magical flowers that react to and purify airborne toxins before they pass through it. While wearing the mask, you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Poisoned condition as well as the effects of magical contagions if they came from an airborne source, and you have Resistance to any Poison damage that those effects might deal.

In addition, the flowers have 3 charges and regain 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn as new flowers bloom. As a Magic action, you can hold the beak's nostrils closed with a free hand and expend 1 charge to exhale a 15-foot Cone of thick pollen in front of you. Each creature in the area must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 2d8 Poison damage, and its Speed is halved until the end of its next turn unless it has Immunity to the Poisoned condition. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only.

This thin blade seems to toe the line between planes of existence, occasionally allowing it to bend the planes to extend beyond its normal reach. You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

The Rapier has 5 charges and regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. When you make a melee attack roll with the Rapier, you can expend 1 charge to extend the weapon, increasing its reach for the attack by 5 feet.

Alternatively, you can expend 1 charge immediately after making a melee attack roll with the Rapier against a target within 5 feet of you, causing the weapon to extend and pierce through the original target. Make an additional melee attack roll with the Rapier against a second target 5 feet behind the original one; the second target must be within 10 feet of you. This additional attack is made as part of the initial attack, and the second target doesn't benefit from using the original one as cover.

Whenever you expend a charge from this weapon, the planes around the extended blade begin to tear, causing the target to take an extra 2d8 Force damage on a hit.

After the attack with the extended blade, it returns to its normal size.

This canister of waxy pomade has magical properties, allowing you to change your hair's color, style, thickness, and length (up to 1 foot longer or shorter per use). The canister steadily replenishes its pomade over time. It can hold up to 4 uses at a time and regains 1d4 expended uses daily at dawn. Applying 1 use of the pomade takes 1 minute.

Once you've used this product in your hair, it returns to its normal appearance after you finish a Long Rest. Hair produced by the pomade that's been cut off turns to dust after 24 hours. If you use the pomade every day for 7 days to make the same changes, the changes become permanent.

Drinking this potion grants you a brief surge of draconic power. Once within the next minute, you can replace one of your attacks when you take the Attack action with an exhalation of magical energy, which has the same effects as the Dragonborn's Breath Weapon trait. The damage type for the exhalation is randomly determined from the Draconic Ancestors table in the Dragonborn species description when this potion is created. The amount of damage the exhalation deals and its save DC are determined by the potion's rarity, as shown in the table below.

If you do, the exhalation's damage type is determined by the kind of dragon the materials were sourced from, and the potion's rarity is determined by the dragon's age category: Uncommon (young dragon), Rare (adult dragon), or Very Rare (ancient dragon). On a failed save, a creature is pushed 10 feet away from you. At the same time, you are flung away, flying 10 feet straight backward without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

This wooden rod is carved in the likeness of five ancient rocs. Motes of their spirits flow through it and allow you to channel some of their lingering power.

This rod has 5 charges and regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. While holding the rod, you can take a Reaction while falling, or a Magic action otherwise, and expend 1 charge to cause two handles to extend from the rod's top and bottom. While holding the handles, a pair of magical wings appear above the rod, slowing your rate of descent to 10 feet per round, or 20 feet per round if you weigh more than 200 pounds. While falling in this way, you can move horizontally or downward as if you had a Fly Speed of 40 feet, but you can't move upward without a significant updraft. If you land while falling in this way, you take no damage from the fall. The wings disappear at the end of the fall, or at the end of your next fall if you summoned them as a Magic action. You can also dismiss them early (no action required).

In addition, while holding the rod aloft, you can take a Magic action and expend 1 charge to summon an instantaneous gust of strong wind. When you do, powerful winds whip around you, blowing things skyward in a 20-foot-radius, 60-foot-high Cylinder centered on a point within 5 feet of you. Large and smaller creatures in the area must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be launched 30 feet upward before crashing back to the ground. Objects in the area that weigh less than 200 pounds are also launched 30 feet upward by the wind. You can choose to automatically succeed on or fail the save. If you choose to fail it and immediately take a Reaction to summon the rod's magical wings, or if they were already summoned, you're launched 60 feet upward instead.

This golden cloak billows illusory sand around you when you walk or cast a spell. The cloak has 8 charges and regains 1d6 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the cloak, you can expend 1 or more charges to cast one of the following spells (save DC 15) from it: Blur (2 charges), Call Lightning (3 charges), Create or Destroy Water (1 charge), or Hallucinatory Terrain (4 charges).

This hat carries with it the cleverness and knowledge of many previous scholars. While wearing it, you gain a +1 bonus to Intelligence checks and Intelligence saving throws. In addition, for every 5 days you spend researching a subject, you gain knowledge as if you had been researching it for 1 additional day.

This hat carries with it the cleverness and knowledge of many previous scholars. While wearing it, you gain a +2 bonus to Intelligence checks and Intelligence saving throws. In addition, for every 5 days you spend researching a subject, you gain knowledge as if you had been researching it for 2 additional days.

You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. This Battleaxe has 8 charges and regains 1d6 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. As long as the weapon has at least 1 charge, attacks you make with it deal an extra 1d6 Fire damage on a hit. When you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll made with this weapon, it regains 3 expended charges.

Erupting Slash

As a Magic action, you can expend 3 or more charges to slash the air in front you with the Battleaxe. When you do, a 5-foot-wide, 30-foot-long Line of fire erupts from the blade. Creatures in the Line must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 1d6 Fire damage for each expended charge. The DC for the save is equal to 8 plus your Proficiency Bonus and the number of charges you expended. If you expend 4+ charges in this way and leave the Battleaxe with 0 remaining charges, the weapon overheats. When it overheats, this effect deals an extra 3d6 Fire damage, and creatures that succeed on the save take half as much damage from the effect.

Arrows fired from this sickly Longbow let out a screeching howl that is audible up to 100 feet away as they streak toward their target. On a hit, the target takes an extra 2d4 Thunder damage. When you roll a 20 on the d20 for an attack roll made with this weapon, the target and each creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or have the Deafened condition for 1 minute.

This golden, twisting hair pin wraps around a tiny silver sword and gives your fingers and skin a slight grip while underwater. Whenever you use the Grapple option of your Unarmed Strikes while you're wearing the pin and are either submerged or swimming in water, the target has Disadvantage on any ability check or saving throw it makes to avoid or end the Grappled condition.

This long captain's jacket carries with it an air of authority. Water slides off of it with ease and magically enhances your comfort in the ocean. While wearing the jacket, you gain a Swim Speed equal to your Speed, and you have proficiency with Navigator's Tools. If you already had proficiency with Navigator's Tools, you have Expertise with them instead.

In addition, you can cast the Fog Cloud spell (level 2 version) from the jacket. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

While wearing this belt and standing on a solid surface, you can begin to sit down in an open space as if there were a chair beneath you. When you do, you can take a Bonus Action to magically summon an Invisible, incorporeal chair, sitting on it instead of crouching or falling to the ground. The chair can be of any style you choose (such as a stool, recliner, throne, or rocking chair) and can support up to 500 pounds. While it is comfortable, it can't be interacted with beyond simply sitting on it. The chair disappears if it is no longer on a solid surface or if you're no longer sitting on it.

This fist-sized, magic seed can be attuned to by four or fewer creatures over the course of a Long Rest. If each creature attuned to the seed participates in gently planting it in fertile soil, the seed immediately begins to flourish, growing into a majestic, flowering tree over the course of 7 days. At the end of that time, the tree is 60 feet tall and 5 feet in diameter at its base, and its canopy extends out in a 30-foot Emanation around the tree. The tree has a number of large limbs equal to the number of creatures attuned to the seed. Once planted in this way, no other creatures can attune to the seed, and the attuned creatures' attunement doesn't end as a result of being more than 100 feet away from the seed for 24 hours or dying. A creature's attunement to the seed immediately ends if it commits a malicious affront to nature.

When a creature attuned to the seed is dead for at least 1 minute, its soul returns to the tree, and its body crumbles into a rich soil that recreates the "enrichment" effect of the Plant Growth spell, centered on the body. The soul returns to the tree regardless of the circumstance of the creature's death or how far away it was from the tree when it died (even if it was on another plane of existence). The returned soul is stored in a shelled nut that the tree grows at the time of the creature's death from the large limb associated with that creature.

After 1d6 + 1 days, the nut falls from the tree and breaks apart, revealing the creature in its new body, as if by the Reincarnate spell. Once a creature is reincarnated in this way, its attunement to the seed ends.

When a creature's attunement to the seed ends, the tree limb associated with that creature withers and dies. The tree is magical and can't be destroyed by nonmagical means. If the tree is destroyed, all creatures attuned to the seed are no longer attuned to it. Any creature attuned to the seed is magically alerted if the tree is being attacked, if it's destroyed, or if one of its large limbs dies. Once all of the tree's large limbs die, the tree splits apart and disintegrates, releasing another Seed of Rebirth to the astral winds that carry it to a new location on a different plane of existence.

You can take a Bonus Action to magically coat this Dart with thick, emerald green poison. The poison remains for 1 minute or until an attack using this weapon hits a creature. That creature must succeed on a DC 13 Constitution saving throw or take an extra 2d8 Poison damage and have the Poisoned condition for 1 minute. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

This necklace can animate small nonliving objects and have them fulfill simple tasks for you. As a Magic action, you can drape or wrap the necklace around a Small or smaller nonmagical object that weighs less than 50 pounds and isn't attached to or carried by anything else. The adorned object springs to life, sprouting little arms and legs, and becomes a mindless creature under your control until you remove the necklace or it takes damage. The servant has an AC of 10 and a Speed of 20 feet.

As a Bonus Action, you can mentally command the servant if it's within 60 feet of you. The servant can perform simple tasks that a Human servant could do, such as fetching things, cleaning, mending, folding clothes, lighting fires, serving food, and pouring wine. The servant can't attack, activate magic items, or carry more than 10 pounds. Once you give it a command, the servant performs the task to the best of its ability until it completes the task, then waits for your next command. If you command the servant to perform a task that would put it in danger or move it more than 60 feet away from you, the servant does nothing.

The necklace can animate an object for up to 8 hours or until it takes damage. When the effect ends, the necklace can't be used again for another 1d8 hours.

This drab pair of empty ceramic cylinders are magically linked. Each tube is 3 inches in diameter and 1 foot tall. Placing an object inside one of the tube and closing its lid creates a quiet whoosh sound as the object is magically teleported to the other tube, which makes a similarly quiet thud. A tube can't send more than 2 pounds of material at a time and can't be used to send a creature. Both tube must be on the same plane of existence and have their lids closed in order for an object to be teleported between them.

This pair of candles are magically linked, and they never seem to run out of wick. They can be used as normal candles, but magically won't light Paper or Parchment on fire.

If you light one of the candles while the other one isn't lit, the first candle begins to burn with a blue flame. By holding a piece of Paper or Parchment over the flame, any nonmagical ink on the page is burnt off, leaving the page unmarked. When you finish using the candle in this way, you can extinguish the flame as normal.

Once the blue flame is extinguished, the linked candle immediately comes alight with a regular orange flame, which smells of lavender and can't be extinguished by nonmagical means. By holding a blank piece of Paper or Parchment over the orange flame, the ink from the first page is magically burnt onto the new one over the course of 1 minute as the candle heats it. Once all the ink has been transcribed onto a new page in this way, the orange flame winks out.
